label_spreading_bootstrap_blocked

Source: R/label_propagation.R
label_spreading_bootstrap_blocked.Rd

Bootstrap label spreading with HDF5 reference and per-cell deviance

Performs multiple label-spreading runs on random subsets of labeled cells, compares each to a full reference solution, and returns the reference probabilities plus mean L1 deviance per cell.

Usage

label_spreading_bootstrap_blocked(
  adj,
  labels,
  alpha = 0.8,
  sample_rate = 0.8,
  sample_n = 50,
  block_size = 128,
  tol = 0.001,
  max_iter = 100,
  epsilon = 0,
  refer_h5 = NULL,
  tmpdir = tempdir(),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

adj

Sparse adjacency (dgCMatrix); will be row-normalized.

labels

Vector of original labels (length \(N\)); mapped once to 1..C.

alpha

Damping parameter for label spreading.

sample_rate

Fraction of labeled cells retained in each bootstrap.

sample_n

Number of bootstrap replicates.

block_size

Classes per block when streaming to HDF5.

tol, max_iter

Convergence parameters.

epsilon

Uniform prior mass added to avoid zeros.

refer_h5

Optional existing reference HDF5 file; if NULL, computed internally.

tmpdir

Directory for temporary HDF5 files.

verbose

Logical; print progress.

Value

A list with:

prob

Dense reference \(N \times C\) probability matrix.

deviance

Per-cell mean L1 deviation vs reference.

Details

- Computes an exact reference with all labeled cells, normalizes it, and stores it in HDF5. - Each bootstrap uses a random subset of labeled cells, writes its results to a temporary HDF5, and accumulates the L1 deviation vs the reference in streaming mode. - Parallelizable via future.apply: set a plan before calling. - A reference created internally is removed on exit. A caller-supplied refer_h5 is treated as a cache and is preserved.

Only intermediate class blocks are disk-backed. The returned prob matrix is dense for compatibility, so callers should still budget roughly \(8NC\) bytes for one final double-precision cells-by-label matrix.

See also

label_spreading_blocked, normalize_hdf5_rows

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(Matrix); library(future.apply)
plan(multisession, workers = 4)
N <- 1000; C <- 4
A <- rsparsematrix(N, N, 0.001); A <- abs(A) + Diagonal(N)
labs <- sample(c(1:C, NA), N, TRUE, prob = c(rep(0.05, C), 0.8))
res <- label_spreading_bootstrap_blocked(A, labs, sample_rate = 0.8, sample_n = 10)
str(res)
} # }
